findings.text: Provides a lookup plus mapping service for a PCI device option ROM. It locates the associated adapter resource and creates an I/O memory mapping over its full extent, returning no mapping when no associated resource exists.
Releases an I/O memory mapping previously obtained for a PCI option ROM image.
Reports the extent of the PCI option ROM associated with a device, reporting zero extent when none is associated.

Boot time firmware ROM discovery. It scans candidate low memory areas for video firmware, then claims the system range, then checks the extension range, then scans adapter ranges on aligned steps, registering each range that shows a valid signature and checksum in the global I/O memory resource tree.
The firmware ROM signature constant equals 0xaa55, checked at the start of every candidate ROM image.

Device identity for option ROM matching holds when vendor and device values equal the requested pair directly, or when the owning driver identifier table contains an entry with that pair. An absent driver or table yields no table match.

Auxiliary list probing walks successive two byte device codes starting at a given list position until a zero terminator. Each nonzero code is tested against the requested vendor under the device identity rule, with faulting reads treated as terminator. Success means a matching code was found.

Option ROM search iterates the adapter resource table in order until an entry with zero end. For each entry it fault safely reads a header offset and vendor and device fields, accepting on direct identity match. Otherwise it fault safely reads a list offset and revision, requiring revision at least three with nonzero list, and accepts when auxiliary list probing succeeds from the computed list position.

All ROM header and content accesses go through a fault safe kernel read helper. Faults during header field reads cause the entry to be skipped, faults during list element reads end the list, and faults during signature or checksum reads cause rejection, so unmapped or vanishing ROM bytes cannot fault the kernel.
Checksum validation sums unsigned bytes over a stated extent and requires both that every byte was readable and that the modulo sum equals zero.

Video firmware discovery steps through low memory in two kilobyte increments between the video base and the first adapter base. The first image showing the signature becomes the video base candidate. Its length byte scaled by five hundred twelve defines a candidate extent that is trusted only when nonzero and checksum valid, after which the video range is registered and the scan stops.

Adapter firmware discovery scans upward from an aligned address derived from the video end toward a dynamic upper bound. Each signature bearing candidate at the current step reads a length byte scaled to an extent, and is recorded only when the extent is nonzero and fits below the bound and checksum passes. Recorded ranges are registered and the scan resumes after the recorded end aligned down to the step size.

Duplicates architecture specific task state from a source task to a destination task, copying the full architecture size with zero padding beyond the generic task size and clearing any VM86 pointer in the destination.
Releases architecture task resources, freeing dynamic floating point state only when dynamic sizing is active and the task is neither a kernel thread nor a user worker.
Thread exit teardown releases I/O bitmap state only when its thread flag is set, then releases VM86 state, shadow stack state and floating point state in order.

Low level fork return path. It first completes the scheduler handoff from the previous task. When a kernel thread function is present it is invoked with its argument and the return register is cleared to allow completion of a kernel execve toward user mode. Control then exits to user mode through the syscall exit path.

Thread creation initializes the child kernel frame to resume at the fork return trampoline with an encoded frame pointer, clears I/O bitmap state and warning and debug breakpoints, copies FS and GS selectors and bases plus legacy segment selectors from current on sixty four bit, sets a fixed flags value and stack top on thirty two bit, allocates a shadow stack top and clones floating point state, then follows distinct kernel thread, user thread with function override, and normal fork paths for register, TLS and I/O bitmap handling.
New TLS selection for a child thread depends on syscall personality, using the thirty two bit area setter with automatic index for compatibility syscalls and the sixty four bit FS setter otherwise.

Thread area installation copies a user descriptor, validates it, resolves automatic index selection and allocation with writeback of the chosen index, enforces TLS index bounds, installs the descriptor, then refreshes live segment selectors when the target is current or updates saved FS and GS bases when the target is another task and its selector matches the modified entry.

TLS descriptor acceptance allows empty or zero descriptors as removal, otherwise rejects sixteen bit segments, rejects non data segment contents, and rejects non present segments, accepting only thirty two bit present data segments.
Free TLS index search returns the lowest numbered empty slot in the current thread array, or a search error when no slot is empty.
TLS descriptor installation pins the current CPU across the update and performs the hardware TLS reload on that same CPU only when modifying the current thread, then releases the pin.

FS and GS preservation always saves selector values. With FSGSBASE support it also reads both bases directly including the inactive GS base. Without that support it leaves zero selector bases untouched as a hot path optimization and clears bases for small nonzero selectors while leaving larger selectors alone.

FS and GS saving for current runs with interrupts disabled. The outer helper saves and restores interrupt state around the save, and inactive GS base reading requires disabled interrupts as verified by an assertion.

Inactive GS base reading takes one of two paths. On non paravirtual systems without flexible return it swaps GS, reads the base, then swaps back. With flexible return or Xen paravirtual support it instead reads the kernel GS base model specific register under instrumentation guards.

Shadow stack thread states move from unallocated through allocated to freed. Allocation is skipped when the feature is off for current, clears tracking and shares the parent stack for virtual fork, reuses the parent copy without new allocation when virtual memory is not shared, and otherwise allocates a new stack recording base and extent and returning its top. Freeing returns early when the feature is off, when address spaces differ or are absent, or when base is null for shared stacks, warns on null extent with set base as double free, otherwise unmaps the recorded range and clears the extent.

Shadow stack sizing aligns any requested size to page granularity, defaulting to the stack resource limit capped at four gigabytes and then aligned. Mapping requests placement above four gigabytes, and optional restore token creation failure releases the fresh mapping and reports an invalid argument.

Restore token creation requires eight byte alignment of the supplied pointer, derives a token address one frame below it, marks the stored value as sixty four bit, writes it to user shadow stack memory, optionally reports the token address, and reports invalid argument on misalignment or fault on write failure.

Shadow stack unmapping treats an interruptible lock failure as imminent process teardown and returns leaving the stack leaked, while any other nonzero result triggers a one time warning, since only memory exhaustion or a bug can cause it.

Per CPU thread state includes boolean flags for invalid TSS limit and incoherent cache state. Per thread shadow stack tracking holds a base address and an extent where null base means no owned stack such as virtual fork sharing, and null extent with set base is abnormal and treated as double free.
Thread creation propagates shadow stack allocation failure as a negative error and aborts the clone, so faulty mapping or token errors prevent a partially initialized thread.
Protection key initialization copies a default value for kernel threads and reads the live hardware value for user threads, since the saved copy is valid only when scheduled out.
